original_test_intent: Verify approved Uncore Configuration controls persist and restore to the platform SPEC while preserving expected UPI, PCIe, cache, NUMA, memory and power-domain initialization and causing no new corrected/uncorrected hardware errors or boot instability.
original_method: Freeze platform/firmware/topology and exact Uncore defaults; preserve logs/counters; select reversible controls with documented affected domains and dependencies; use KVM to change one control or coherent group, save/reboot and capture retained values; after each boot compare UPI/PCIe link topology, NUMA/memory inventory, cache/frequency/power indicators and RAS deltas; apply Load Defaults and repeat comparisons; stop at first link loss, topology change, error burst or no-boot and recover with owner-controlled known-good/CMOS procedure.
manual_activity: A qualified operator navigates the Uncore page, applies only approved values, performs controlled save/reboot and Load Defaults cycles, captures every screen, and maintains physical/KVM recovery access.
required_inputs: Platform/BIOS/microcode identity plus socket, UPI, PCIe, memory and NUMA baseline
Complete Uncore default oracle and safe value matrix with affected domain/dependency/expected effect
Maintenance, KVM, known-good settings, BIOS/CMOS recovery ownership and physical access
safety_requirements: Qualify each Uncore value; never change all/random settings
Preserve SEL, AER, EDAC/MCA and performance/topology counters; use timestamped baselines rather than clearing
Change one control/group and verify every affected domain before continuing
Stop on UPI/PCIe downgrade/loss, NUMA/memory change, RAS delta, thermal/power anomaly, hang or no-boot
Do not auto-reboot, retry or clear CMOS
agent_execution_scope: Validate identity, Uncore defaults/matrix, dependencies, expected effects, evidence and recovery
Guide operator checkpoints and organize screenshots plus UPI/PCIe/NUMA/memory/cache/frequency/power/RAS comparisons
Verify retention and restoration against SPEC without issuing the hardware verdict
Do not select values, clear evidence, navigate/save BIOS autonomously or invoke recovery
engineer_actions: Approve exact Uncore page/defaults and per-setting reversible matrix with domain/dependency expectations
Approve topology/performance/RAS acceptance, reboot timing, Load-Defaults scope and recovery
Review BIOS, boot, link/topology and error evidence and decide PASS, FAIL, or BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Interactive BIOS operation has no SSH substitute; DeepSeek's manual boundary fits. Post-boot tools can only corroborate UPI/PCIe/NUMA/memory/cache/power state after operator actions.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Operator performs the approved Uncore matrix and default restore through KVM; the agent collects non-destructive hardware-topology, link, RAS and firmware evidence at each checkpoint.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Uncore page persistence/default sequence and 5/20-minute allocation remain; `all/random` is not executable authorization.

modernized_recommendation.status: HIGH MANUAL UNCORE PERSISTENCE, TOPOLOGY AND DEFAULT-RESTORE TEST
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use a domain-aware incremental matrix and pair page screenshots with link/topology, cache/frequency/power and RAS comparisons after every reboot and restore.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds Uncore-specific subsystem oracles, counter preservation, incremental fault isolation and recoverable stop points.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A system may boot and retain the selected value while silently degrading UPI/PCIe width/speed, memory/NUMA topology, cache behavior or power/performance policy.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Uncore changes can destabilize inter-socket links, I/O fabric and memory domains, creating no-boot, hidden performance loss or hardware errors.

project_override_considerations: Auto/default semantics can depend on CPU stepping, population and BIOS build; record resolved effective state, not only the menu token. Project recipe defaults may differ from firmware factory defaults and must be explicitly named.
expected_evidence: Exact row/variant/hash, approval and platform/BIOS/microcode/topology identity
Uncore SPEC/project defaults, selected values, dependencies and affected-domain rationale
Timestamped baseline, changed, retained, Load-Defaults and restored screenshots
Per-phase UPI/PCIe link, NUMA/memory, cache/frequency/power and boot/readiness comparisons
Preserved SEL/AER/EDAC/MCA/kernel evidence and delta analysis

engineering_decision_pending.question: Resolve Functionality row 2178 Wistron-BIOS-00495-V004: approve platform/BIOS/microcode identity, exact Uncore page and SPEC/project defaults; safe reversible values, dependencies and expected UPI/PCIe/cache/NUMA/memory/power effects replacing `all/random`; link/topology/performance/RAS and reboot criteria, log/counter preservation, Load-Defaults scope, aborts, and KVM/physical/CMOS recovery ownership.

review_improvement: Adds Uncore-specific link, topology, performance and RAS validation, so a retained menu value cannot hide degraded fabric behavior and random low-level combinations cannot strand the platform.
independent_technical_reasoning: Uncore settings govern shared fabric rather than only a local menu state. Their effective result depends on CPU stepping and population, and failures may appear as reduced link width/speed, altered NUMA or memory visibility, RAS events or performance/power shifts while the system still boots. A valid review therefore binds each value to its affected-domain oracle and preserved counters. Physical KVM and manual recovery remain mandatory because an unsafe Uncore value can block pre-OS progress.
